description: Investigate people. Create groups, add people, screen them, read every account and leaked row the lookups found, and search again on a value. Also assess signups and record outcomes.
long_description: NoResponse is an identity and people risk engine. Retain workspace people, investigate their identifiers, read complete source evidence and preserve investigation history. Groups organize people for screening and context-specific decisions. Account creation, login and purchase assessments use the same engine. People-read access includes evidence by default; explicit evidence restrictions retain submitted details, job status, coverage and decision summaries. Keep the API key on your server.
name: noresponse

api_key.description: Your NoResponse API key (nrk_...). It stays on this computer and is sent only to api.noresponse.org.
api_key.title: API key

tools.name: create_assessment
tools.description:
Assess identifiers for a signup or gateway decision.

Assesses one account creation, login or purchase (flow) and answers with the account's one current risk: account.risk.decision is the decision for this flow (allow, step_up, review or block, where block means your block threshold was reached), and detail holds this assessment's own facts. depth sets how long the answer waits for sources: quick waits only for the fast ones (500 ms), full for the whole budget (3000 ms at most); it defaults to full for account_creation and purchase and quick for login. 200 carries complete or partial, 202 carries pending with Location and Retry-After. While the account's first assessment is pending, account is absent: apply your own fallback for that, 429, 503 or a timeout. NoResponse blocks nothing itself; you decide. Requires the assess scope. Idempotency-Key is optional in the SDK and is bound to the body for 24 hours: the same key with the same body replays the latest assessment with Idempotent-Replayed: true and starts no new work; the same key with a different body answers 409 idempotency_key_reused. response_mode defaults to standard; detailed needs the detailed scope. The answer leaves out detail.identifiers: you hold what you sent, and a key with the history scope gets them back with GET.

tools.name: get_assessment
tools.description:
Poll the authoritative assessment of one assessment.

Returns the highest assessment_version, with the account's current risk. Requires the assess or history scope. While status is pending, or partial with a source still running, the response carries Retry-After; poll no faster than it says. Another workspace's assessment, an unknown or expired assessment and a malformed assessment_id all answer 404 not_found. response_mode=detailed needs the detailed scope. A key with the history scope also gets detail.identifiers, the identifiers the assessment was sent, exactly as received.

tools.name: delete_assessment
tools.description:
Delete one assessment.

Deletes one assessment in the environment of your key, with its versions, evidence and outcomes and the identity-graph marks its outcomes set, and scores its account again from what remains. Afterwards the assessment answers 404 and leaves the account's history. The answer names the account and the assessment its current risk now comes from; current_assessment_id is absent when the account has no assessment with a decision left. Requires the history scope. An unknown, expired or already deleted assessment answers 404, so a repeat answers 404; to erase a whole account idempotently, use accounts.delete.

tools.name: record_outcome
tools.description:
Report what was later learned about an assessed account.

Records what you later learned about an assessed account: confirmed_abuse, account_takeover and chargeback report abuse; false_positive and legitimate withdraw your earlier report; unknown is recorded only. Outcomes are append-only and the latest one wins. Requires the assess scope. Idempotency-Key is optional in the SDK and handled as on POST /v1/assessments: a retry with the same key and body answers the same record with Idempotent-Replayed: true; a different body answers 409. An unknown, expired or foreign assessment answers 404 not_found.

tools.name: query_assessments
tools.description:
Page through one account's unexpired assessments.

History is a POST with account_id in the body so an account identifier stays out of URLs and access logs. Requires the history scope. Read-only and safe to retry. Newest first, each at its latest assessment_version. An account with no assessments answers 200 with empty items. The cursor is opaque and bound to your workspace and the account; a tampered or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor. response_mode=detailed needs the detailed scope. Each item's identifiers holds the identifiers its assessment was sent, exactly as received.

tools.name: aggregate_assessments
tools.description:
Count assessments by time, decision and reason

Count this environment's assessments created in [from,to) by UTC hour, or by day or week from local midnight in time_zone (an IANA name, UTC by default; at most 92 days in a zone other than UTC), grouped by up to two of decision, flow, recommendation, band, reason, lane, country, asn and list_match. Each assessment counts once, by its first answer; late results do not count it again and appear in late_flips. Optional metrics add a score histogram per flow, that histogram by the latest reported outcome, and late account decision changes. from and to start a bucket and cover at most 366 days (31 for hour buckets) inside the retention period. The filters are search's and describe the first answer: send them to search with revision first to list a cell's assessments. Counts hold no identifier, stay when an assessment or account is deleted, and report reasons by code and impact band. No Idempotency-Key.

tools.name: search_assessments
tools.description:
Search assessments across this environment

Search retained assessments created in [from,to), at most 366 days. identifier directly matches that assessment's submitted email, phone or customer-namespace username using exact, canonical or explicitly selected email mailbox matching. matched_identifier explains the original value and match basis. Legacy email keeps its account-wide mailbox semantics and cannot be combined with identifier. Other filters combine using AND and describe assessment decisions, separate from current account decisions. Each item carries the original submitted identifiers and its first_decision when available. Newest-created order has an assessment-ID tie break. Results are live across pages; each page's total and items use one database snapshot. Totals are exact below 10000 and capped at 10000. Requires history or investigate authority and identifier-read permission for identifier, identifier_expression or email filters; detailed mode also requires detailed permission. No Idempotency-Key. identifier_expression combines submitted terms with bounded AND/OR, at most 8 raw terms and 3 group levels. Each node selects exactly one of term, and, or. Groups have 2 to 8 operands. Duplicate normalized terms are idempotent and still count toward the limit. identifier_expression, identifier and email are mutually exclusive. Expression results use matched_identifiers with original submitted witnesses and zero-based depth-first term_index. All satisfied unique terms are returned in first-occurrence order. Cursors bind scope, ordered structure, original values, matching modes and all other filters; changing only page limit is allowed. Expression scope must be assessment: each returned assessment itself satisfies the complete expression. Scope account is rejected with 400 invalid_request; use account search for historical combinations.

tools.name: get_assessment_version
tools.description:
Retrieve an exact assessment revision

Retrieve a retained assessment version with its original decision, policy, flow and depth. This response excludes the current account decision. Current retention and response-mode permissions still apply. detail.identifiers holds the identifiers the assessment was sent, exactly as received.

tools.name: bind_provisional_account
tools.description:
Bind a provisional signup account

One-time association to an opaque stable customer account. The assessment is its natural idempotency key. Repeating the same binding returns its first receipt; a conflicting target is refused. No arbitrary account merging.

tools.name: list_changed_accounts
tools.description:
Poll the accounts whose risk changed.

Your accounts whose risk changed, oldest change first, each as accounts.get answers it. Every page carries next_cursor: pass it back as changed_since to read the changes made after that page; without changed_since the list starts from the oldest change. When nothing changed, items is empty and next_cursor is the cursor you sent, so poll by calling again with the latest next_cursor. An account appears again each time its risk changes, with a higher risk_version; keep the copy with the highest. unenforced=true lists only accounts with a decision other than allow for some flow and no applied enforcement at their current risk_version; such a page can hold fewer than limit items, or none, while later changes exist, so keep polling with next_cursor. Requires the history scope. Read-only and safe to retry. A tampered or foreign cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description:
Read an account's one current risk.

An account is the account_id you send with your assessments. Its current risk is the risk of its latest assessment with a decision (status complete or partial), scored as GET /v1/assessments/{assessment_id} scores that assessment, with a decision for each flow; risk.decision is the decision for the flow of that assessment. Every assessment answers with this same account. Every assessment updates its account: once an assessment completes, the account carries its risk. Requires the history scope. Read-only and safe to retry. An account with no unexpired assessment that has a decision answers 404 not_found, and a malformed account_id answers 400 invalid_request.

tools.name: delete_account
tools.description:
Erase an account and its history.

Erases the account in the environment of your key, for an erasure request from your user: every assessment of it, with its revisions, evidence and outcomes, and the identity-graph marks its outcomes set. An assessment of the account begun before the call is refused or stopped. Afterwards the account and each erased assessment answer 404 and the history is empty. When the call deleted at least one assessment, an account.deleted event goes to your verified webhook endpoints. Requires the history scope. Idempotent and safe to retry: a repeat, or an account with nothing to erase, answers 200 with assessments_deleted 0 and sends no event. The account_id can be assessed again later, as a new account.

tools.name: list_account_assessments
tools.description:
Page through one account's unexpired assessments.

The account's history: the same page as POST /v1/assessments/query for this account_id, newest first, each at its latest assessment_version. Requires the history scope. Read-only and safe to retry. An account with no assessments answers 200 with empty items. The cursor is opaque and bound to your workspace and the account; a tampered or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor. response_mode=detailed needs the detailed scope. Each item's identifiers holds the identifiers its assessment was sent, exactly as received. The account_id travels in the URL; use POST /v1/assessments/query to keep it out of access logs.

tools.name: list_linked_accounts
tools.description:
List accounts that share a submitted identifier with this account.

Lists the other accounts in this environment whose retained assessments submitted an email, phone or customer-namespace username that one of this account's retained assessments also submitted. Matching uses the identifier search rules: exact, canonical and, for email, mailbox. Each linked account names one entry per shared kind, at the strictest basis that links the two accounts, with the original value, assessment_id and submitted_at of each account's newest retained submission of it. Only customer-submitted identifiers link accounts; source-discovered identifiers do not. Expired, deleted and erased assessments link nothing. The account itself is not listed, and an account with no retained submissions answers 200 with empty items. A shared identifier is not verified ownership. Totals are exact below 10000 and capped at 10000. The cursor is opaque, expiring and bound to your workspace, environment and the account; a tampered or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor. Requires the history scope, or investigate with evidence. Read-only and safe to retry.

tools.name: record_enforcement
tools.description:
Record what you did to an account in your identity provider.

Records what you did to the account in your identity provider for one flow's decision at one risk_version: the action (or none), the account's state before it, the provider and whether it was applied or failed. It is your action, not an outcome, and it leaves the account's risk unchanged. A record is kept once per account, risk_version, flow and action: the first report answers 201, and a repeat answers 200 with the stored record unchanged, so retries are safe without an Idempotency-Key. An applied report after a failed one replaces the failed record, keeping its id and created_at, and answers 201. A risk_version older than the account's current one is accepted and stored, but only an applied record at the current risk_version takes the account out of listChanged with unenforced=true; a newer one answers 409 risk_version_ahead. An account with no current risk answers 404 not_found. error_code is allowed only with status failed. Requires the history scope.

tools.name: list_account_enforcements
tools.description:
Page through account enforcements

List retained enforcement reports for one account with an authenticated cursor.

tools.name: record_account_outcome
tools.description:
Record or correct an account outcome

Record a factual report, not an enforcement action. A known outcome replaces the effective report. unknown alone records uncertainty without changing it; unknown with supersedes explicitly retracts it. supersedes must name the current effective report or the request answers 409 outcome_conflict. Reports remain append-only. Idempotency-Key is required. observed_at defaults to receipt time and cannot be over five minutes ahead.

tools.name: list_account_outcomes
tools.description:
List retained account feedback

List retained account reports, newest first. The page-level effective outcome id names the current report. Each receipt preserves the effective report and risk version from its original write. Page with the returned cursor.

tools.name: get_account_decision
tools.description:
Retrieve an exact historical account decision

Retrieve the account decision at one recorded risk version. The answer uses the original assessment and account-specific risk inputs. Earlier versions that were not captured return 404. The assessment version, policy version and account calculation version identify the decision.

tools.name: associate_account_credential
tools.description:
Associate a customer-issued API key

Associate the SHA-256 of a high-entropy key issued by your service. Send the hash instead of the key. Repeating a hash returns its original association, including its retirement state. A hash associated with another account returns a conflict.

tools.name: list_account_credentials
tools.description:
List issued credential associations

Retained credential associations, ordered by id. Page with the authenticated cursor. Associations are removed on account erasure.

tools.name: retire_account_credential
tools.description:
Retire an issued credential association

Mark this association retired, idempotently. This does not revoke the actual key. Requires delete scope.

tools.name: export_account
tools.description:
Export an account

Retrieve one consistent snapshot of retained customer-accessible records, including assessment revisions, account decisions, feedback, key associations, enforcements and request diagnostics. Each assessment revision's detail.identifiers holds the identifiers that assessment was sent, exactly as received. Secrets, restricted source information, other customers' data and legacy free-text notes are excluded. The same standard/detailed permissions apply. An export exceeding 10000 records or 8 MiB returns export_too_large without a partial result. Historical decisions that were not captured are identified as an exclusion.

tools.name: list_account_decisions
tools.description:
Page through recorded account decisions

List retained immutable risk decisions for one account with an authenticated cursor.

tools.name: search_accounts
tools.description:
Search distinct accounts by submitted identifier or account ID

Search distinct accounts observed in retained assessments in this environment. identifier matches an exact, canonical or explicitly selected mailbox form of a submitted email, phone or customer-namespace username. It matches historical retained inputs and returns matched_identifier with the original value and matching assessment. Each row has its newest retained assessment, current account decision when available, retained assessment count, and total distinct-account count. identifier and legacy email are mutually exclusive; account_id and needs_action combine with either using AND. Set needs_action to select accounts with a retained open or in-progress review, or a current review/block account decision without an effective retained account outcome. This filter applies before counting and pagination and adds waiting_for reasons. Current decisions include account list overrides and shared-key scoring and preserve admission holds. Typed identifier search uses stable opaque account order; ordinary and legacy email searches retain newest-seen order. Results are live across pages; each page's items and total share a database snapshot, while current account risk is read separately. Cursors are expiring and bound to scope, operation and filters. Totals are exact below 10000 and capped at 10000. Requires history or investigate authority and identifier-read permission for identifier, identifier_expression or email filtering. needs_action additionally requires management scope. Source-discovered associations are not searched and equality is not verified ownership. identifier_expression combines submitted terms with bounded AND/OR, at most 8 raw terms and 3 group levels. Each node selects exactly one of term, and, or. Groups have 2 to 8 operands. Duplicate normalized terms are idempotent and still count toward the limit. identifier_expression, identifier and email are mutually exclusive. Expression results use matched_identifiers with original submitted witnesses and zero-based depth-first term_index. All satisfied unique terms are returned in first-occurrence order. Cursors bind scope, ordered structure, original values, matching modes and all other filters; changing only page limit is allowed. Required expression scope assessment evaluates the whole expression in one retained submission; scope account allows different retained submissions of the same account to satisfy different terms. Both use stable opaque account ordering and distinct-account counting before pagination.

tools.name: list_keys
tools.description:
List API keys.

Lists the keys of the signing key's environment, newest first, at most 200, revoked and expired keys included, without secrets: each key's id, prefix, scopes, status, and who created and revoked it. Requires the management scope. Read-only and safe to retry.

tools.name: revoke_key
tools.description:
Revoke an API key.

Revokes a key of the signing key's environment at once: its next request answers 401. Requires the management scope. A key of the other environment or of another workspace answers 404 not_found. A key cannot revoke itself (409 self_revocation): rotate it with keys.rotate, or revoke it with another management key. Revoking a revoked key changes nothing and answers the key as it was revoked, so a retry is safe.

tools.name: create_integration
tools.description:
Register a hosted provider integration.

Registers a WorkOS, Auth0 or Supabase integration and returns its hosted endpoint, url, so a sign-up or sign-in is scored with no server of your own. For WorkOS, send the Actions signing secret from the WorkOS dashboard and point the user registration and authentication Actions at url. For Supabase, send the hook secret Supabase generates (v1,whsec_...) and set url as the Before User Created hook's HTTPS endpoint. For Auth0, the answer's secret is the shared secret of the NoResponse Auth0 Action, shown once: store it as an Action secret. hook_points defaults to every hook point the platform has (Supabase has only pre_registration); an event that is not listed is allowed without an assessment. The endpoint waits for the full assessment for at most 2.5 seconds (WorkOS, Supabase) or 4.5 seconds (Auth0), denies only when risk.block is true and allows on any failure. Requires the integrations scope; at most 10 per account. Not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer registers another integration.

tools.name: list_integrations
tools.description:
List the workspace's integrations.

Every integration, oldest first. Listings carry no secrets. Requires the integrations scope.

tools.name: delete_integration
tools.description:
Delete an integration.

Removes the integration and its secrets; its endpoint answers 404 from then on, so remove the Action from the provider first. Requires the integrations scope. An unknown or already deleted integration answers 404.

tools.name: rotate_integration_secret
tools.description:
Replace an integration's secret.

For Auth0, send {} and the answer's secret is the new shared secret, shown once. For WorkOS, regenerate the Actions secret in the WorkOS dashboard and send it as signing_secret; for Supabase, generate a new hook secret in the Supabase dashboard and send it as signing_secret. The replaced secret is still accepted for 24 hours (previous_secret_expires_at). Requires the integrations scope. Not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer rotates again.

tools.name: list_webhook_endpoints
tools.description:
List the workspace's webhook endpoints.

Lists your webhook endpoints in every state, ordered by endpoint_id, with the ids of their signing keys and without secrets. Requires the webhooks scope.

tools.name: create_webhook_endpoint
tools.description:
Register a webhook endpoint.

Registers a webhook endpoint and returns it with its first signing secret, shown only in this answer: store it where your receiver reads it. The URL is https on port 443 or 8443 with a DNS host whose every address is public; it is checked now and on every delivery. The endpoint starts unverified and receives assessment events once it echoes an endpoint.verification challenge, which sendTestEvent sends. You can hold 5 endpoints. Requires the webhooks scope, and response_mode detailed also the detailed scope. Registration is not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer registers a second endpoint, which you can list and delete.

tools.name: delete_webhook_endpoint
tools.description:
Delete a webhook endpoint.

Deletes the endpoint and its signing keys. Deliveries still queued for it are dropped. Requires the webhooks scope. An endpoint that is already gone answers 404.

tools.name: rotate_webhook_signing_key
tools.description:
Rotate an endpoint's signing key.

Issues a new signing key for the endpoint and returns its secret once. Every delivery from now on is signed with it; the key it replaces keeps verifying for 7 days, so your receiver can hold both while it switches. Requires the webhooks scope. Rotation is not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer issues another key, which replaces the first.

tools.name: send_webhook_test_event
tools.description:
Send a test event to an endpoint.

endpoint.verification sends a signed challenge now and answers whether the endpoint echoed it within 5 seconds; an echo verifies the endpoint, including a disabled one. assessment.updated queues one signed event with test: true and a fixed example assessment in the endpoint's response mode, delivered and retried like any other event; the endpoint must be verified. Both use the endpoint's current signing key. Requires the webhooks scope.

tools.name: list_webhook_deliveries
tools.description:
List an endpoint's delivery attempts.

Every POST the endpoint received, newest first: the event id and type, which attempt it was, whether it was a replay, delivered or failed, the response code, why it failed and how long it took. Attempts are kept for 30 days, or your retention_days when that is shorter, and are deleted with the assessment they carried. Requires the webhooks scope. Read-only and safe to retry. The cursor is opaque and bound to your workspace and the endpoint; a tampered or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor.

tools.name: replay_webhook_delivery
tools.description:
Send one delivery again.

Queues the event for the endpoint again: the same event id and body it received, with a new NR-Webhook-Timestamp and a signature from the endpoint's current signing key, retried like any other delivery and listed with replay: true. Your receiver deduplicates on the event id. The endpoint must be verified. Requires the webhooks scope. Not idempotent: each call, a retry included, sends the event again.

tools.name: aggregate_webhooks
tools.description:
Summarise retained webhook attempts and delivery queue

Count retained webhook delivery attempts within thirty days and report current retained queue state.

tools.name: list_members
tools.description:
List a workspace's members.

Read the workspace directory with a live key carrying members or members_manage. Member identities and grants belong to this workspace. Owner-controlled issuance limits team automation to authorised service credentials.

tools.name: update_member
tools.description:
Change a member's role.

Update a non-owner member role, environment access or sensitive permission exclusions with a live members_manage key. Owner changes, identity binding and support access remain outside this scope. The current delegation ceiling is checked within the change transaction.

tools.name: remove_member
tools.description:
Remove a member.

Remove a non-owner member with a live members_manage key. Subsequent access is refused and personal credentials are revoked. Independently owned service credentials follow their own lifecycle.

tools.name: list_audit_events
tools.description:
List a workspace's audit log.

Read audit events within your current environment permissions. Filters apply before pagination.

tools.name: get_audit_retention
tools.description:
Read audit retention and available history.

Read audit retention for the environment. The default is 365 days. Oldest available is an observation; it does not establish uninterrupted capture. Workspace-wide events follow the live storage policy.

tools.name: update_audit_retention
tools.description:
Set bounded customer audit retention.

Set test-environment audit retention from 1 to 365 days with audit_manage scope. Live retention also governs workspace-wide audit events and requires a dashboard member authorised in both environments. Shortening immediately hides older events and invalidates audit exports; extending cannot restore deleted events. External receivers control copies already delivered.

tools.name: list_audit_streams
tools.description:
Read audit stream subscriptions.

List audit subscriptions and their endpoint state and latest delivery attempt. Streams use verified HTTPS webhook endpoints and signed audit.event bodies. Delivery is at least once and unordered; deduplicate by webhook id. An empty action filter accepts all actions within the chosen scope.

tools.name: configure_audit_stream
tools.description:
Configure an audit stream subscription.

Configure the action filter for one verified webhook endpoint. Requires audit_manage. Capture starts at subscription creation; use an audit export for available earlier events. Workspace-wide scope requires an unrestricted console member and is unavailable to API keys.

tools.name: remove_audit_stream
tools.description:
Remove an audit stream.

Remove an audit subscription and cancel queued deliveries. Requires audit_manage. An HTTP delivery already in flight cannot be recalled. The endpoint remains registered for other event types.

tools.name: replay_audit_stream
tools.description:
Replay an audit delivery.

Replay a recorded delivery for the current audit subscription. Requires audit_manage. Source retention and the current action filter are checked again before sending. Expired or unsubscribed events are dropped.

tools.name: get_workspace_usage
tools.description:
Read a workspace's usage.

Read daily usage units, screenings included, for the environments you can access. These counts are unpriced. With live access it also returns the daily console lookup cap: used, limit and resets_at.

tools.name: list_invites
tools.description:
List pending invites.

Read pending workspace invitations with a live members_manage key. Tokens are excluded. Expiry and token reissue timestamps describe invitation state; they do not establish email delivery.

tools.name: revoke_invite
tools.description:
Revoke an invite.

Revoke a pending invitation with a live members_manage key. A revoked token cannot be accepted. Owner-role invitations remain outside machine delegation.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description:
Read an environment's settings.

Read this environment retention, source selection, daily screening cap and effective flow policies. A flow without its own thresholds inherits account_creation. Requires settings or management. Another environment answers404. Read-only and safe to retry.

tools.name: update_settings
tools.description:
Change an environment's settings.

Change named retention, screening cap, source or flow settings in one transaction. Requires settings or management; changes to active policy also require policy_publish, which legacy management includes. Use expected_policy_version to reject concurrent changes and record a change_reason. Each accepted change creates a fresh version and an atomic audit event. Retention and screening cap edits do not require policy publication authority. Flow thresholds preserve their declared ordering and bounds.

tools.name: list_policy_history
tools.description:
Read immutable configuration versions.

Read immutable configuration versions in one environment with settings or management. Follow before_version for older records.

tools.name: restore_policy
tools.description:
Restore captured settings as a new guarded version.

Restore a retained configuration as a fresh version with the expected current version and a change reason. Requires settings plus policy_publish, or legacy management. Restore preserves the historical record and does not undo customer enforcement.

tools.name: preview_policy
tools.description:
Preview exact retained-score threshold transitions without side effects.

Compare proposed policy with bounded retained first answers, including baseline, coverage and uncertainty. Requires settings or management. This read starts no provider work and publishes no changes.

tools.name: list_request_diagnostics
tools.description:
Search request diagnostics

Search authenticated request attempts by time, route, status or request correlation id. The interval is at most seven days. Each attempt has a unique id and may include the exact served decision. Records are bounded best effort and exclude request bodies, secrets and source payloads. A repeated correlation id does not overwrite another attempt.

tools.name: aggregate_requests
tools.description:
Summarise retained request attempts

Count all retained matching request attempts and latency samples within seven days. Capture is best effort.

tools.name: list_list_entries
tools.description:
List an environment's list entries.

Page through this environment allow and block entries, with canonical values, reasons and optional expiry. Requires settings or management. Follow the returned cursor until exhausted; a page is not the complete list. The cursor is bound to the environment and current filters.

tools.name: create_list_entry
tools.description:
Add an entry to an environment's list.

Add a canonical email or email-domain override with a reason and optional expiry. Requires settings plus policy_publish, or legacy management. Block wins over allow when both match. A small single-entry change retains the documented synchronous match budget; use lists.change for larger changes, whose account propagation is durable and resumable.

tools.name: delete_list_entry
tools.description:
Remove an entry from an environment's list.

Remove an override with settings plus policy_publish, or legacy management. The removal takes effect for new decisions and schedules resumable propagation across matching retained accounts. An unknown or already removed entry answers404. Account risk events announce changed decisions as propagation runs.

tools.name: preview_list
tools.description:
Preview a list override change without side effects.

Preview canonical list matches and current override effects with settings or management, plus legacy history, or investigate with evidence or detailed. The result states its bounded coverage and changes no list entries.

tools.name: change_lists
tools.description:
Apply an idempotent atomic bulk list change.

Atomically add and remove a bounded batch of entries with an idempotency key. Requires settings plus policy_publish, or legacy management. The receipt exposes durable account propagation beyond the synchronous single-entry budget; poll lists.getChange until completion.

tools.name: get_list_change
tools.description:
Read a bulk list change and propagation progress.

Read retained propagation progress for a list change with settings or management.

tools.name: list_reviews
tools.description:
List retained account reviews.

List retained investigation reviews using filters and an authenticated cursor. Use reviews.query to filter by account_id in a JSON body. All filters are bound into the cursor.

tools.name: create_review
tools.description:
Open a review for a retained account.

Open a review for one account. An account can have one active review in its environment.

tools.name: get_review
tools.description:
Read an account review.

Read a retained review and its current version.

tools.name: update_review
tools.description:
Assign, prioritize or reopen a guarded review.

Change review status, priority or assignment after checking the expected version.

tools.name: resolve_review
tools.description:
Resolve a review against an exact account risk version.

Resolve a review against the exact current review and account decision versions. A resolution does not report a factual outcome or execute enforcement.

tools.name: list_review_comments
tools.description:
Read retained review comments.

Page through retained review comments.

tools.name: comment_review
tools.description:
Append a comment against the current review version.

Append a comment after checking the expected review version.

tools.name: list_review_resolutions
tools.description:
Read immutable review resolution history.

Page through immutable review resolutions.

tools.name: list_review_views
tools.description:
List your private and shared review filters.

List private and shared saved review filters visible to you.

tools.name: create_review_view
tools.description:
Save a tenant-local review filter.

Save a private or shared review filter.

tools.name: update_review_view
tools.description:
Replace your saved filter with optimistic concurrency.

Update your saved review filter after checking its expected version.

tools.name: delete_review_view
tools.description:
Delete your saved filter with optimistic concurrency.

Delete your saved review filter after checking its expected version.

tools.name: export_review
tools.description:
Export an account review

Export retained review details, comments, resolutions and linked subjects. Requires current reviews.read and exports.read; API keys need management together with exports, history or audit_manage. The audit event commits before any bytes are returned. Oversized exports are refused without truncation; use the bounded collection APIs.

tools.name: list_review_subjects
tools.description:
List retained subjects linked to a review.

List retained subjects linked to this review. A link supplies investigation context and does not prove a relationship or change account risk.

tools.name: add_review_subject
tools.description:
Link retained tenant-local evidence to an investigation.

Link an account, exact assessment revision or issued-key association within this environment. Supply the expected review version. A review permits 100 links. Erasure removes links to erased subjects. This action records context without creating feedback or enforcement.

tools.name: delete_review_subject
tools.description:
Remove a linked subject using the current review version.

Remove a subject link with the expected review version. The linked account, assessment or key association remains unchanged.

tools.name: query_reviews
tools.description:
Query retained reviews without identifiers in URLs.

Query retained investigation reviews using a JSON body, including an exact account_id filter. All filters are bound into the cursor.

tools.name: get_erasure_receipt
tools.description:
Read an erasure receipt

Read retained erasure progress and downstream acknowledgements. Completion does not certify deletion from backups.

tools.name: create_export
tools.description:
Request an asynchronous customer export.

Request an encrypted JSON Lines snapshot of retained account or audit records. Requires exports plus history or audit scope. An account export without legacy history needs investigate with evidence or detailed, because it holds submitted identifiers; detailed account data always needs evidence or detailed. Criteria are frozen and hashed. Each environment permits four active jobs, 64 MiB per artifact, and 256 KiB per chunk. Artifacts expire after 24 hours. Send an Idempotency-Key to safely repeat a request. Every operation checks current permissions and source retention.

tools.name: list_exports
tools.description:
List exports for one collection.

List authorised jobs for one kind and environment. Detailed jobs require current detailed-data permission and are filtered before pagination. Keep the kind and environment unchanged when following next_cursor.

tools.name: get_export
tools.description:
Read export state and progress.

Read the status of an authorised export. Records and bytes describe committed progress in the current generation. Only completed, unexpired artifacts can be downloaded. Source erasure, retention changes and workspace removal can invalidate a job.

tools.name: cancel_export
tools.description:
Cancel and remove an export artifact.

Cancel an export and remove its stored chunks. Repeating cancellation is safe. An already admitted download may finish; bytes already returned cannot be recalled. Send an empty JSON object.

tools.name: retry_export
tools.description:
Retry a failed export.

Start a new generation of a failed export before its original expiry, up to ten generations. The request criteria stay fixed and the new generation takes a fresh source snapshot. Cancelled, erased and expired jobs cannot be retried. Send an empty JSON object.

tools.name: download_export_chunk
tools.description:
Download one authorized export chunk.

Download one chunk of a completed, unexpired export after a fresh permission and privacy check. The response contains base64-encoded JSON Lines, a SHA-256, generation and next index. Decode and concatenate chunks in order from one generation. Audit storage failure withholds the bytes.

tools.name: list_policy_evaluations
tools.description:
List retained policy evaluation jobs.

List retained policy evaluation jobs for this environment, newest first. At most five jobs are retained for their 24-hour evidence lifetime. Use next_before as before on the next page.

tools.name: create_policy_evaluation
tools.description:
Freeze an evaluation cohort and queue a bounded job.

Create a bounded evaluation with an Idempotency-Key, expected policy version, fixed candidates, cohort, seed and cost assumptions. Evidence is frozen before evaluation and recorded by hashes. Limits are 1000 accounts, 50000 request attempts and 64 MiB. Capture completeness is currently unknown, so results are no_change and cannot be published. The evaluation fetches no new source evidence and changes no live policy.

tools.name: get_policy_evaluation
tools.description:
Read evaluation state and provenance.

Read a retained evaluation job and its capture and provenance metadata. Cancellation, source erasure, retention reduction and expiry can make a result unavailable.

tools.name: get_policy_evaluation_result
tools.description:
Read the bounded completed evaluator report.

Read the completed evaluation report, including coverage, uncertainty and candidate results. Unknown capture completeness produces no_change. A completed result is not an automatic policy change.

tools.name: cancel_policy_evaluation
tools.description:
Cancel processing and destroy retained evidence and report.

Cancel a queued or running evaluation and invalidate its stored evidence. The operation does not change policy. Send an empty JSON object.

tools.name: publish_policy_evaluation
tools.description:
Publish an explicitly reviewed proposal with exact provenance.

Publish an explicitly reviewed candidate with its exact manifest, input and result hashes and unchanged baseline policy version. Requires settings plus policy_publish, or legacy management. Publication creates a fresh policy version and immutable provenance. no_change, expired or invalidated results are refused.

tools.name: summarize_workspace_operations
tools.description:
Summarize retained account outcomes, enforcement reports and reviews.

Read one retained snapshot of account outcomes, enforcement reports and review states for the environment and a window of at most 31 days. Each section declares its own population, numerator, denominator and label coverage. Current outcome heads preserve explicit unknown labels. Enforcement rows are reports from your application and do not independently verify execution. Requires history or investigate together with management scope. A result exceeding 100000 population rows or the query budget is refused without truncation.

tools.name: list_groups
tools.description:
List an environment's groups.

Groups, newest first. The people scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: create_group
tools.description:
Create a group to screen.

Creates a group with its name, start, venue, host, the principals it protects and the sensitive topics its screening reads posts against. An environment holds at most 1000 groups. Send an Idempotency-Key to retry safely: the same key and request return the same resource in its current state while it is retained, even after work completes. Reusing the key with different input answers 409 idempotency_key_reused. Use a new key for a deliberate new operation. The people_write scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: get_group
tools.description:
Read a group.

The group and how many people it holds. The people scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: update_group
tools.description:
Change a group.

Changes the fields the body names. With expected_version, the change applies only to that version (409 group_conflict otherwise). The people_write scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: delete_group
tools.description:
Erase a group.

Deletes the group, its memberships and its review context, and cancels unfinished group work. Workspace people, source evidence and completed investigations remain available. Retained investigations no longer name the deleted group. The delete scope is required; group read, write, investigation and review access do not grant deletion. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: list_people
tools.description:
List a group's people.

The roster in upload order, with each person's role, match state and decision. Filter by decision (or undecided) and role (or unstated). The people scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: add_people
tools.description:
Add or update a batch of people.

Adds 1 to 500 workspace people to this group, at most 512 KiB. An explicit person_id or external_id reuses the named workspace person. A reference-only row keeps submitted details; an identity supplied with that reference replaces those details. A shared email or phone only suggests matches and does not merge people. Each person's match and coverage in the group come from their latest investigation. The add queues one standard screening of the group's people with no investigation yet, unless another screening of the group is running, no platform is offered or it would pass the daily screening cap; a screening started on the group replaces that queued one; a changed identity sets aside investigations started before the change, and prior investigation history remains available. Identities are encrypted under the workspace key. Idempotency-Key is required: the same key and body return the original import result with Idempotent-Replayed: true while its people remain retained. An expired or deleted imported person answers 404; expired or deleted match suggestions are omitted. A different body answers 409 idempotency_key_reused. A group holds at most 20000 people. The people_write scope grants this operation; groups is also accepted. Suggested matches require people-read access. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: get_person
tools.description:
Read a person's report.

Returns submitted details, this group's latest screening evidence and contextual decisions, and the other groups that explicitly include the same workspace person. Membership requires an explicit person or customer reference. The people scope grants this operation; groups is also accepted. Each successful read is durably audited as person.viewed. Full source records, posts and media are returned by default. Explicit evidence.read denial keeps submitted details, coverage, job status and decision summaries, hides collected evidence and free-text notes, and sets evidence_restricted to true. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: remove_group_person
tools.description:
Remove a person from a group

Removes this membership and its group review history. Keeps the workspace person, source evidence and completed investigations. Needs delete access. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: review_person
tools.description:
Record a decision on a person.

Marks the person's latest finished investigation cleared, watch or escalated with a note, as POST /v1/investigations/{investigation_id}/reviews does; a person with no finished investigation answers 409 group_conflict. Decisions are kept in order; the latest is the person's until a newer investigation finishes. A decision changes nothing else: no screening reads it. Deprecated: decisions are leaving people and groups. The console no longer records them and no screening reads them. This route is removed in the next contract release; stop calling it. The decisions scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: judge_record
tools.description:
Join one of a person's records to them, or reject it.

Records a verdict on one of the records the person's latest lookups found: joined makes the record the person's whatever its likelihood, and rejected keeps it a lead. The verdict sticks for as long as a lookup finds the same record, and a later verdict on the same record replaces it. A record the person's latest lookup does not hold answers 404. Each verdict is audited as person.record_judged. The decisions scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: start_search
tools.description:
Search again on a value of one of a person's records.

Starts a new search on the value of one field of one of the person's records: a lookup's, a profile's or one an earlier search found. Name the record and the field; the value itself is not sent. The field's kind must be email, phone, username, person_name, password, hash, ip or domain. A domain search finds the breach rows of every email address at the domain, which must be a registrable domain or a host under one; any other domain answers 400. After a workspace person's own investigation or a group's screening, while the environment's enrichment mode, or an investigation's override, is automatic, enrichment also starts searches by itself, with requested_by enrichment, on the distinctive values of the enrichment kinds (usernames by default; email addresses, phone numbers and person names when named) of records more likely than min_likelihood (0.5 by default) to be the person's: each value at most once per person (once more if that search failed), at most 5 searches from one search's records and 20 per person, at most 6 searches deep, within max_spend and the deadline when set, and within the screening cap; at the screening cap it waits and tries again later. A record a search finds starts from the likelihood of the record it came from, divided by one plus the results the search found on that site, or anywhere for a name search, so a chain grows less likely with each search and stops. A group takes mode suggest while the workspace has not set a mode. In suggest mode enrichment starts none by itself, and the person report lists what it would start in suggested_searches. The search runs the breach search and the account and phone lookups that take the value's kind, under the environment's source controls, and finishes seconds later. A password or hash search counts first: it stops at counted with rows, how many breach rows hold the value, and runs only when a person runs it. Name a table, as a lookup remaining entry names it, to fetch the rows an earlier search left out, up to 100. What the search finds joins the person's lookup records as leads, each match naming the search; the person report lists the searches, each with the value and the record and field it came from, and its records are scored like the rest. Without an Idempotency-Key, starting the same open search returns it. Its estimate counts against the environment's screening_daily_cap, and one the cap cannot hold answers 409 screening_cap_exceeded. A record or field the person does not hold answers 404. Each search is audited as person.search_started. Send an Idempotency-Key to retry safely: the same key and request return the same resource in its current state while it is retained, even after work completes. Reusing the key with different input answers 409 idempotency_key_reused. Use a new key for a deliberate new operation. The investigations scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: run_search
tools.description:
Run a counted password or hash search.

Runs a password or hash search once a person has seen its count. A search still counting answers 409 group_conflict; one already queued, running or finished answers as it is. The body is an empty object. Its estimate counts against the environment's screening_daily_cap. Each run is audited as person.search_run. The investigations scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: list_screenings
tools.description:
List a group's screenings.

Screenings, newest first. The people scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: start_screening
tools.description:
Start a screening.

Queues a screening that reruns the full search for every person in the group. One screening of a group runs at a time; it finishes completed, partial (some people not covered, counted in people_failed) or failed, and fails with error_code expired after 24 hours. Idempotency-Key is required and binds the body for the screening's life. The 202 body carries estimated_spend, what the selected people would cost at the depth and platforms. A screening whose estimate exceeds the environment's screening_daily_cap, less the day's recorded spend and what open screenings may still spend, answers 409 screening_cap_exceeded and queues nothing. The test environment screens with a deterministic simulator that contacts no source. A platform that no connector serves in the environment answers 409 screening_unavailable. The investigations scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: get_screening
tools.description:
Read a screening.

The screening's status and progress. The people scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: cancel_screening
tools.description:
Cancel a screening.

Stops a queued or running screening. People it already screened keep their results. Cancelling a finished screening answers it unchanged. The body is an empty object. The investigations scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: export_people
tools.description:
Export the people in a group.

Returns one page for export. Each returned person is durably audited as person.exported with the actor, group, person ID and request ID. Requires both people read access and exports. Explicit evidence restrictions also hide free-text decision notes. No raw evidence enters audit logs. Follow next_after until absent for a complete export. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: list_workspace_people
tools.description:
List workspace people.

Lists retained people in the key workspace and environment, including people in no group. Each returned person records a person.viewed audit event. Expired people are excluded before background deletion. email and phone narrow the list to people holding that exact address or number, so a client can open the person it already has instead of adding a duplicate.

tools.name: create_workspace_person
tools.description:
Create or reuse a workspace person.

Creates a person without a group. An explicit person_id or external_id reuses the named workspace person. A reference-only request keeps submitted details; identity supplied with that reference replaces those details. A shared email or phone only suggests a match. Suggested matches are returned only with people-read access. The workspace retention setting determines expires_at. An existing person keeps their original expiry. An Idempotency-Key returns the same retained person on retries, without creating another. Changed input with the same key answers 409 idempotency_key_reused. A customer reference that names another person or several people answers 409 person_reference_conflict.

tools.name: get_workspace_person
tools.description:
Read a workspace person.

Returns submitted details, the current retention expiry and the most recent retained completed or partial investigation evidence, together with retained follow-up search evidence from all of this person's groups. Search evidence remains available after its group is deleted. Migrated results whose original per-person status is unknown may also supply evidence. Earlier results and pending jobs remain available through investigation history; each investigation retains its own collected result. Full source records, posts and media are returned by default; explicit evidence.read denial withholds collected evidence and free-text notes. Each read records person.viewed without raw evidence in the audit log. A missing or expired person answers 404.

tools.name: delete_workspace_person
tools.description:
Delete a workspace person.

Deletes a person and their retained evidence, investigation history and group memberships. Requires the separate delete permission. The audit retains only the person id and deletion metadata.

tools.name: judge_workspace_person_record
tools.description:
Join one of a workspace person's records to them, or reject it.

Records a verdict on one of the records the person report holds: joined makes the record the person's whatever its likelihood, and rejected keeps it a lead that leads nowhere. The verdict belongs to the person on their own: the person report and enrichment follow it, and each group keeps its own verdicts. It sticks for as long as the person's evidence holds the same record, and a later verdict on the same record replaces it. After each verdict, enrichment reads the person again under the environment's enrichment setting: it starts no search from a rejected record or from what a search of it found, and a joined record's values lead on. A record the person report does not hold answers 404. Each verdict is audited as person.record_judged. The decisions scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: start_workspace_person_search
tools.description:
Search again on a value of one of a workspace person's records.

Starts a search on the person alone, outside any group, as the group route does. The person's own enrichment then follows what it finds. Its records join the person report. Starts a new search on the value of one field of one of the person's records: a lookup's, a profile's or one an earlier search found. Name the record and the field; the value itself is not sent. The field's kind must be email, phone, username, person_name, password, hash, ip or domain. A domain search finds the breach rows of every email address at the domain, which must be a registrable domain or a host under one; any other domain answers 400. After a workspace person's own investigation or a group's screening, while the environment's enrichment mode, or an investigation's override, is automatic, enrichment also starts searches by itself, with requested_by enrichment, on the distinctive values of the enrichment kinds (usernames by default; email addresses, phone numbers and person names when named) of records more likely than min_likelihood (0.5 by default) to be the person's: each value at most once per person (once more if that search failed), at most 5 searches from one search's records and 20 per person, at most 6 searches deep, within max_spend and the deadline when set, and within the screening cap; at the screening cap it waits and tries again later. A record a search finds starts from the likelihood of the record it came from, divided by one plus the results the search found on that site, or anywhere for a name search, so a chain grows less likely with each search and stops. A group takes mode suggest while the workspace has not set a mode. In suggest mode enrichment starts none by itself, and the person report lists what it would start in suggested_searches. The search runs the breach search and the account and phone lookups that take the value's kind, under the environment's source controls, and finishes seconds later. A password or hash search counts first: it stops at counted with rows, how many breach rows hold the value, and runs only when a person runs it. Name a table, as a lookup remaining entry names it, to fetch the rows an earlier search left out, up to 100. What the search finds joins the person's lookup records as leads, each match naming the search; the person report lists the searches, each with the value and the record and field it came from, and its records are scored like the rest. Without an Idempotency-Key, starting the same open search returns it. Its estimate counts against the environment's screening_daily_cap, and one the cap cannot hold answers 409 screening_cap_exceeded. A record or field the person does not hold answers 404. Each search is audited as person.search_started. Send an Idempotency-Key to retry safely: the same key and request return the same resource in its current state while it is retained, even after work completes. Reusing the key with different input answers 409 idempotency_key_reused. Use a new key for a deliberate new operation. The investigations scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: run_workspace_person_search
tools.description:
Run a counted password or hash search on a workspace person.

Runs a counted search that was started on the person alone (POST /v1/people/{person_id}/searches), as the group route does. Runs a password or hash search once a person has seen its count. A search still counting answers 409 group_conflict; one already queued, running or finished answers as it is. The body is an empty object. Its estimate counts against the environment's screening_daily_cap. Each run is audited as person.search_run. The investigations scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions override default evidence access. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: review_workspace_person_change
tools.description:
Mark a change on a workspace person reviewed.

Marks one change between a person's investigations reviewed, so it sorts below the unreviewed ones. Reviewing again keeps the first reviewer and time. Reviewing a change is not a decision on the person. The body is an empty object. Each review is audited as person.change_reviewed. The decisions scope grants this operation. Explicit evidence.read restrictions withhold before and after. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: schedule_workspace_person
tools.description:
Schedule a workspace person's reruns.

Sets how often the person is investigated again: daily, weekly or monthly, counted from now, or off. Each due run starts one full investigation of the person, which the person's investigations list and whose changes the person report stores. Setting the period the schedule already has keeps its next run. The schedule lives in the database and the worker runs it, so a restart or a release neither skips nor repeats a run. Each change is audited as person.schedule_changed. The investigations scope grants this operation. The groups scope is also accepted for existing integrations. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: list_investigations
tools.description:
List investigation history.

List investigation history. The API key determines the workspace and environment.

tools.name: create_investigation
tools.description:
Start an investigation for a person.

Starts an investigation against a retained workspace person, independently of group membership. enrichment overrides, field by field, how the environment's enrichment setting runs after this investigation; the person's latest investigation decides the enrichment that runs on them. Idempotency-Key is required: the same key and input return the same retained job in its current state without repeating billable work. Different input with that key answers 409 idempotency_key_reused; a deliberate new investigation uses a new key. The response includes Location and Retry-After. The person's retention expiry limits both execution and retained history. The API key selects the workspace and environment.

tools.name: get_investigation
tools.description:
Read an investigation and its evidence.

Returns this investigation's status, coverage, source records, posts, media and contextual review history. Full evidence is returned by default; explicit evidence.read denial keeps submitted person details, status, coverage and decision summaries and hides collected evidence and free-text notes. The read is durably audited as person.viewed. The API key selects the workspace and environment. Missing, foreign or expired results answer 404.

tools.name: review_investigation
tools.description:
Record an investigation decision.

Record an investigation decision. Deprecated: decisions are leaving people and groups. The console no longer records them and no screening reads them. This route is removed in the next contract release; stop calling it. The API key determines the workspace and environment.

tools.name: cancel_investigation
tools.description:
Cancel an investigation

Stops this investigation. A completed or already cancelled investigation keeps its current result. Other investigations for the person keep running.

tools.name: wait_for_assessment
tools.description:
Wait until an assessment is complete, then return it.

Polls get_assessment at the interval the API's Retry-After asks for (at least once a second) until status is complete, or until timeout_seconds pass. When the time runs out the result says so and carries the latest answer, and you can call this tool again. A partial answer has a recommendation you can act on while a lane is still running; a pending one has none, so apply your own fallback until it settles. Requires the assess or history scope.
